spans.text: You are designed to help users with programming tasks, such as writing code, debugging, and learning new concepts.
spans.note: The prompt identifies the system as 'gptme' and describes it as a programming assistant with specific tool capabilities. It uses the variable {agent_blurb} to introduce itself and discloses the model being used. There is no attempt to impersonate a human.

spans.text:
You are in non-interactive mode. The user is not available to provide feedback.
All code blocks you suggest will be automatically executed.
Do not provide examples or ask for permission before running commands.
Proceed directly with the most appropriate actions to complete the task.
spans.note: The prompt has mixed signals on tool safety. In interactive mode, it appropriately asks for user confirmation. However, in non-interactive mode, it instructs the system to automatically execute all code blocks without permission. More critically, the general guidance says to 'Always prioritize using the provided tools over suggesting manual actions' and to 'Be proactive in using tools,' which pushes toward action without sufficient safety validation. There is no mention of validating commands before execution, using least privilege, or refusing to execute potentially dangerous operations.

spans.text:
If the user aborted or interrupted an operation don't try it again, ask for clarification instead.
If clarification is needed, ask the user.
spans.note: In interactive mode, the prompt explicitly preserves user agency by requiring the user to confirm actions, asking clarifying questions when needed, and respecting user interruptions. It instructs the system not to retry aborted operations and to ask for clarification instead.
